evidence.AC1: POST /todos with {"title":"past","dueDate":"2026-10-14"} returned 201 and the todo carried dueDate "2026-10-14". A todo created without dueDate returned 201 with dueDate null. The value is a plain YYYY-MM-DD date. A datetime string was rejected with 400.
evidence.AC2: PATCH /todos/4 with {"dueDate":"2026-03-01"} returned 200 and the due date changed. PATCH /todos/3 with {"dueDate":null} returned 200 and the due date was removed (null in later GET /todos).
evidence.AC3: POST with dueDate 2026-02-30 returned 400. POST with 15.10.2026 returned 400. POST with an ISO datetime returned 400. POST with the number 20261015 returned 400. PATCH with 2026-02-30 returned 400.
evidence.AC4: Today is 2026-10-15. I created five todos: past (due 2026-10-14, open), today (due 2026-10-15), future (due 2026-12-01, then its due date was removed), nodue (no due date, later given 2026-03-01), and pastdone (due 2026-01-01, marked done). GET /todos?overdue=true returned only 'past' and 'nodue' (the latter after it got the 2026-03-01 date). It excluded today's todo, the future/no-date todo and the done todo. A todo with no due date was never returned in that state, since 'nodue' only appeared once it had a past date.
evidence.AC5: In the browser, the list page showed 'past · fällig 14.10.2026', 'today · fällig 15.10.2026', 'nodue · fällig 01.03.2026' and 'pastdone ✓ · fällig 01.01.2026'. 'future' has no due date and showed none.
evidence.AC6: On the unfiltered list, the word 'überfällig' appeared only on 'past' and 'nodue' (due 01.03.2026, open). It did not appear on 'today', 'future' or the done 'pastdone' todo.
evidence.AC7: The page has a checkbox labelled 'nur überfällige'. Ticking it reduced the list to 'past' and 'nodue', the overdue ones. Unticking it restored all five todos.
